subheading: DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSES OF GONORRHEA IN CHILDREN
subheading_corrected: DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSES OF GONORRHEA IN CHILDREN
text:
Differential Diagnoses
- The silver nitrate prophylaxis can produce a chemical conjunctivitis,
usually appearing 6 -8 hours after treatment and resolving over 24 hours
- The most common cause of neonatal conjunctivitis in most countries is C.
trachomatis, E. coli, Staphylococci, Streptococci and Pseudomonas sp. can
also cause conjunctivitis in the neonate.
